overview: This bill protects veterans and others who attend college or training programs using Post-9/11 GI Bill benefits, the main education benefit run by the Department of Veterans Affairs. It bars schools from refusing to release the official academic transcript of such a student just because the student owes the school money. Without a transcript, a person can have trouble transferring to another school or proving their education to an employer. As of September 24, 2026, a House committee had approved an amended version and it was awaiting action by the full House.
for: Supporters say holding transcripts hostage over debts, sometimes caused by delays or changes in GI Bill payments, can block veterans from continuing their education or getting jobs.
against: Critics say schools lose one of their few practical ways to collect money they are owed, which could raise costs or lead schools to pursue debts in other ways.
